Notes: First mention of Jewish community 1551 (Polish Diet at Wilna); evidence of Jews as early as 1490
Evidence that Jews lived in Polotsk as early as 1490 (toward end of 15th century)
Ivan the Terrible captured Polotsk; about 300 Jews who refused baptism drowned in the Dvina (event count)
Magdeburg Rights charter included edict against Jews depriving them of right to trade and build or buy houses; Jews present
478 Jewish families; Estimate based on families
10797 Jews (53.1% of 20321 inhabitants) reported as non-Christian/Judaism adherents
1897 census; 61.5% of population; 23 synagogues and talmud torah in early 20th century
October 1905 pogroms; authorities prohibited Jewish self-defense; organized community with 23 synagogues talmud torah and Jewish high school
German occupation 16 July 1941; ghetto of approx 2500 inmates; about 100 Jews shot Aug 1941; 2300 Jews shot 21 Nov 1941
December 1941 7000 Jews of Polotsk and its environs murdered (includes environs)
Second half of 1940s about 3000 Jews lived in Polotsk; midpoint 1946 used; source says ok. 3 tys. (approximate)
